reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that economic systems are not neutral but embody moral structures. Predatory acquisition and social production form a dualistic framework where the former often dominates under certain institutional regimes. This duality manifests in how labor is deployed—either toward productive ends or destructive ones. The mathematical lens captures this through antagonistic variables A_p and A_s, which define a phase space where moral character M = A_p - A_s determines systemic health. When predatory activity exceeds productive capacity, the system enters a destabilizing regime. The GSI mapping formalizes this as a Bayesian risk model where moral outcomes are inferred from behavioral data. In GSE, this translates into agent-based simulations where moral conflict drives state transitions. The failure mode occurs when predatory activity is optimized without constraint, leading to systemic collapse.
